added_meaning: Selected exact House floor State Homeland Security Grant Program and Stonegarden funding follow. House floor 60005 common appropriation: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury, not otherwise appropriated, to be administered under the State Homeland Security Grant Program authorized under section 2004 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 605), to enhance State, local, and Tribal security through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, and other activities, of which-- House floor 60005 purpose 1: $500,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for State and local capabilities to detect, identify, track, or monitor threats from unmanned aircraft systems (as such term is defined in section 44801 of title 49, United States Code); House floor 60005 purpose 2: $625,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2026 FIFA World Cup; House floor 60005 purpose 3: $1,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2028 Olympic Games and 2028 Paralympic Games; and House floor 60005 purpose 4: $450,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for the Operation Stonegarden Grant Program. The pre-vote fiscal year 2024 DHS/FEMA HSGP notice reproduced on Hawaii's official host describes Operation Stonegarden as supporting enhanced cooperation and coordination among CBP, USBP, and Federal, State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies to improve overall border security. It funds joint border-security efforts along routes of ingress and egress to and from international borders, including travel corridors in States bordering Mexico and Canada and States and territories with international water borders. In that notice, those State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies use their inherent law enforcement authorities and receive no additional authority from participating in Stonegarden. This is dated program-purpose context, not a new power conferred by the House appropriation or a complete 2025 eligibility rule. The floor clause appropriates to the FEMA Administrator additional fiscal year 2025 funds administered under the State Homeland Security Grant Program in 6 U.S.C. 605 for State/local/Tribal security through the printed grant, contract, cooperative-agreement and other activity paths. Each of its four purpose amounts has its own availability until September 30, 2029. The Stonegarden amount is $450,000,000. House FIFA purpose (2) expressly includes planning; House purpose (3) expressly names the 2028 Olympic Games and 2028 Paralympic Games. The Senate prints different event wording; no decision about either version's actual event-expense eligibility is inferred. The House selected text prints no Senate 90005(a)(2) FIFA/Olympics exemption or added consistent-with-titles-18-and-49 phrase. That absence is a source-version comparison, not authority to disregard otherwise applicable law. Generic drone and event funding remain adjacent context without an inferred Immigration purpose. Complete captured 603, 605 and 609 and the dated program notice are reused without changing earlier Senate meanings or declaring their every condition automatically applicable to a House-version grant. House-specific application question 53 remains separate from Senate question 52. No particular grant, entitlement, expenditure, law-enforcement power or individual status result is inferred. The floor 60005 operative body is identical to the currently governed EH 60006 body after section-title labels are removed solely for comparison. Exact adopted H.Res.492/499 witnesses contain no direct textual change to this clause; they are retained as correction-chain context, not evidence that the full served EH equals the vote-time bill. Earlier floor authority and raw source versions remain unchanged. Other package components and previously reserved questions remain unfinished.

Res. 499 In the House of Representatives, U. S., June 11, 2025. Resolved, That upon adoption of this resolution it shall be in order to consider in the House the bill (H.R. 4) to rescind certain budget authority proposed to be rescinded in special messages transmitted to the Congress by the President on June 3, 2025, in accordance with section 1012(a) of the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974. All points of order against consideration of the bill are waived. The bill shall be considered as read. All points of order against provisions in the bill are waived. The previous question shall be considered as ordered on the bill and on any amendment thereto to final passage without intervening motion except: (1) one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Majority Leader and the Minority Leader or their respective designees; and (2) one motion to recommit. Sec. 2. The provisions of section 1017 of the Impoundment Control Act of 1974 shall not apply to a bill or joint resolution introduced with respect to the special message transmitted under section 1012 of that Act on June 3, 2025. Sec. 3. House Resolution 492 is hereby adopted. Attest: Clerk.
